newsitem.title: USA: Key Republican calls U.S. utilities 'disingenuous'.
newsitem.headline: Key Republican calls U.S. utilities 'disingenuous'.

text.p: House Commerce Committee Chairman Tom Bliley on Tuesday accused U.S. electric utilities of making "phony" arguments in their fight against federal legislation to make states open local power markets to competition.

Pointing to lawsuits brought by utilities in New Hampshire, Arizona and New York challenging state moves to break up utility monopolies, Bliley, a Virginia Republican, said the companies were being "two-faced" in fighting for states' rights in Congress.
"In Washington, the electric monopolies holler that federal legislation to give consumers a choice in electricity is a violation of States' Rights," he said in a statement.
"But in courtrooms all around the country, the utilities' lawyers are saying that unless we change federal law, the States don't have the power to allow competition on their own," he said.

"Maybe electric utilities' high-paid Washington spin doctors ought to talk to their even higher-paid lawyers, but either way, these lawsuits expose the utilities' States Rights argument as phony and disingenuous," Bliley said.
Bliley has said that electric market deregulation was one of his top priorities this year. The House energy and power subcommittee is set to hold its first hearing on a deregulation bill on June 17.
